question: Why does measuring one entangled electron instantly affect the other, light-years away?
answer: After two electrons interact, they no longer have separate wave functions; one wave function describes both. Measuring either electron collapses that whole wave function, so the other is set at the same instant, however far away.
move: Entangled means one wave function for two particles: collapse it anywhere, it collapses everywhere.

web.label: Two electron pictures that merge into one shared, interconnected web when tapped. The question asks why measuring one entangled electron instantly affects the other, light-years away.
